chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya and al-Husayn ibn ʿUbayd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from ʿUmar ibn Yazid, who said:
ʿAmr ibn Saʿid ibn Hilal narrated to me, saying: I asked Aba Jaʿfar عليه السلام about what falls into the well, from a mouse and a cat up to a sheep,
So he said: “For all of that, seven buckets are prescribed.” He said: until I reached the donkey and the camel, and he said: “A kurr of water.”

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: If a sheep, a dog, a pig, a cat, a gazelle, a fox, and the like of its body-size dies in it, forty buckets are drawn from it. If a pigeon, a chicken, or what resembles them dies in it, seven buckets are drawn from it. That indicates this.

key_terms.السِّنَّوْرِ: a cat, mentioned among the animals affecting well water
key_terms.الشَّاةِ: a sheep, used as an upper limit in one part of the ruling
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse, mentioned as a smaller animal falling into the well
key_terms.خِنْزِيرٌ: a pig, one of the animals mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.دِلَاءٍ: buckets of water to be drawn from the well
key_terms.كُرٌّ: a fixed large measure of water required in this context
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: is drawn out, referring to removing water from the well

ai.seo_question: How much water must be drawn from a well if different animals fall into it or die in it according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses legal rulings concerning the purification of well water when animals fall into it or die in it. It specifies different amounts of water to be drawn depending on the size and type of the animal, reflecting detailed fiqh rulings on ritual purity and najasah.
